Do not fail me.|Alecia Beck|''[[Smuggler's Run: A Han Solo & Chewbacca Adventure]]''}} '''Stormtroopers''' ('''STs''')—also known as '''Imperial stormtroopers''' and often derogatorally referred to as "'''bucketheads'''"—were the elite shock [[troop]]s of the [[Galactic Empire]], and were part of the [[Stormtrooper Corps]], an independent [[Imperial Military|military]] branch operating under the [[Imperial Army]]. These elite, obedient and zealous [[soldier]]s wore [[Stormtrooper armor|armor]] consisting of [[Color|white]] [[plastoid]] [[Armor|plates]] over a black [[body glove]], and their standard issue weapon was the [[E-11 medium blaster rifle]]. In addition to the standard variant [[trooper]], various specialized units such as [[scout trooper]]s and [[Cold weather assault trooper|snowtroopers]] comprised the ranks of the [[corps]]. Alongside [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] and [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]], stormtroopers served as reminders of the absolute power of the Empire. In addition, stormtroopers would serve with the [[Imperial Army trooper|regular]] [[Imperial Navy Trooper|infantry]] to enforce [[Imperial Era|oppressive rule]] over the [[galaxy]]. Taking their name from the "storm" of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]], [[clone trooper]]s served as the first generation of stormtroopers, and were gradually replaced by Imperial recruits known as [[TK stormtrooper]]s. Clone troopers were composed of the [[Cloning|clones]] who formed the backbone of the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] from its [[Empire Day|inception]] at the [[Mission to Mustafar|end]] of the [[Clone Wars]] when the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]] [[Proclamation of the New Order|declared]] the [[Galactic Republic]] at an end and himself [[Galactic Emperor]]. Into the early [[Standard year|years]] of the Imperial Era, the [[cloning]] operation on [[Kamino]] was shut down as the Empire turned to conscription and voluntary recruitment in order to fill the stormtrooper ranks. The remaining clones were gradually retired from service due to their rapid aging, their legacy inherited by [[Reproduction|natural-born]] [[human]]s who were also trained to render total allegiance to the [[Emperor]] and his [[New Order]]. Stormtroopers were spread throughout galaxy, from the galactic [[capital]] of [[Coruscant]] in the [[Core Worlds]], to major installations and vital [[List of planets|worlds]], enforcing widespread terror and mass oppression. These infantry fought many battles against the [[Alliance Military|forces]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]], including the [[Battle of Scarif]], the [[Battle of Hoth]], and the Battle of [[Endor]]. Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin]], [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] was [[Secret mission to Tatooine|captured]] by stormtroopers who served under the [[Emperor's Fist|Emperor's lieutenant]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. However, Organa was [[Rescue of Princess Leia|rescued]] by [[Luke Skywalker]] and [[Han Solo]] who, disguised as stormtroopers, infiltrated the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|first Death Star]]. The Emperor stationed a [[legion]] of stormtroopers on Endor to protect the [[Death Star's shield generator|shield generator]] of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]], although they were defeated by the Alliance's [[Ewok]] allies. With the [[death]]s of Emperor Palpatine and [[Lord]] Vader, [[Counselor to the Empire]] [[Gallius Rax]] took control of the Empire, which rallied to his [[homeworld]] of [[Jakku]] to make a final stand against the [[New Republic]] during the [[Battle of Jakku]], however the Empire [[Galactic Concordance|collapsed]], with its replacement of the New Republic consequently demobilizing stormtrooper forces. Despite being illegal, a number of '''Remnant Stormtroopers''' remained active as soldiers or [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] for [[warlord]] factions, including [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]'s [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|forces]] as well as the [[Morak Imperial remnants|remnants]] on [[Morak]]. By the [[Cold War|last days]] of the [[New Republic Era]], a [[First Order stormtrooper|new generation of stormtroopers]] emerged from the [[Unknown Regions]] as standard soldiers of the [[First Order]]. ==History== ===Origin=== {{Quote|The storm of history. As the galaxy transitioned from chaos to order, our regiment was created to maintain that order.|Stormtrooper [[Crag]] gives an account of the origin of the name "stormtrooper"|{{StoryCite|story=Born in the Storm|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} [[File:Acme-FollowingOrders.png|thumb|left|300px|Stormtroopers were modeled on the clone troopers who fought for the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars and were made to turn on the Jedi under Order 66.]] At the [[Proclamation of the New Order|dawn]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the first generation of stormtroopers consisted of [[Cloning|cloned]] [[soldier]]s who served the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars]].''[[Star Wars: Meet the Villains: Stormtroopers]]'' Under the leadership of the [[Jedi Knight]]s, [[clone trooper]]s fought the [[Separatist Droid Army|droid armies]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] across [[the galaxy]]. Though they were loyal to the [[Jedi]] as well as the Republic, the clones were secretly [[Behavioral modification biochip|programmed]] to obey [[Order 66]],{{Databank|clone-troopers|Clone Troopers}} a [[Republic Military|military]] [[Executive Order Codes for the Grand Army of the Republic|directive]] authorizing the complete [[Great Jedi Purge|liquidation]] of the [[Jedi Order]].{{TCW|Shattered}} With the exception of a handful of survivors,''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' including [[Jedi General]]s [[Yoda]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], most of the Jedi were [[Death|killed]] by their own [[troop]]s at the command of [[Darth Sidious]], the [[Sith Lord]] who orchestrated the Clone Wars and controlled the [[Galactic Senate]] through his secret identity of [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine.{{Film|III}} With the Empire claiming the [[galaxy]] was brought from chaos to order during to its rule, one account of the origins of the name "stormtrooper" was that it came from the troopers emerging from the "storm" of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]]. Another origin came from the final [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Republic Era]]: with [[Imperial shock trooper|clone shock troopers]] enforcing law on the Republic capital of [[Coruscant]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' and taking the role once held by the [[Senate Guard]],{{Databank|coruscant-guard|Coruscant Guard}} onlookers began to refer to the soldiers as "stormtroopers." ===Ending the clone trooper program=== {{Main|Clone trooper}} {{Quote|Surely you realize the precarious state this newly formed Empire is in. Clone troopers will be needed to maintain order throughout the galaxy.''"
"''Indeed. A service conscription soldiers could provide at half the cost.''"
"''The skill level and efficiency of our clones is far superior to that of any recruited body.|Lama Su and Wilhuff Tarkin|{{TBB|Aftermath (episode)}}}} [[File:Andor-Clones-point-blasters.png|thumb|right|300px|After the Clone Wars, the remaining clone troopers became the first stormtroopers of the Galactic Empire.]] Renamed "stormtroopers" and assigned their new role by [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Palpatine himself,''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Death Star Deluxe Book and 3D Wood Model]]'' the clone [[trooper]]s enforced his reign during the early [[Standard year|years]] of the [[Imperial Era]] No longer beholden to the authority of Jedi [[officer]]s who exercised restraint in warfare{{TCW|Innocents of Ryloth}}{{TCW|Counterattack}} and with their loyalty enforced by their control chips, the clones utilized brutal tactics under the leadership of [[Imperial officer]]s and [[Governor]]s, suppressing dissent and imposing the [[New Order]] over the known galaxy as the first generation of Imperial stormtroopers. Immediately, the Empire moved to remove sedition within its [[Imperial Senate|legislative branch]], as clones were deployed to carry out the [[Senatorial arrests]], rounding up a total of sixty-three [[senator]]s who were subsequently claimed to be Jedi sympathizers.''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' The end of the Clone Wars, however, fulfilled the sole purpose behind the creation of clone troopers. Although Palpatine supported the [[Ruling Council (Kamino)|Kaminoan government]]’s clone trooper program during his final years as Supreme Chancellor, his priorities changed from the expensive cloning production after aponting himself Galactic Emperor. The [[Prime Minister]] of [[Kamino]], [[Lama Su]], maintained that the clone troopers possessed unrivaled combat skills and discipline. In addition, Lama Su believed that his clones were critical to the security of the fledgling Empire. Despite this, Governor and [[Admiral]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] was confident the Empire would be better served by a force of recruits, which he saw as a cost-effective way to enforce order in the galaxy. [[File:TRF_Senatorial_arrests_fixed.png|thumb|left|250px|Clone troopers would enforce Imperial control over the galaxy, eliminating any threats to the new regime.]] In addition, there were further incentives for the Empire to decommission its clone units in favor of [[Reproduction|natural-born]] [[human]]s. The clones' accelerated aging process limited their "shelf-life."''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' Further, their original purpose as soldiers of the now-replaced Republic made Imperial higher-ups uncomfortable.{{TBB|War-Mantle}} Tarkin himself had noticed the individuality clones had developed under Jedi leadership, which made them unpredictable for Imperial purposes. As such, Tarkin sought a clean break from the Jedi-influenced past.{{TBB|The Summit}} Although Tarkin supported conscription and recruitment over cloning,{{TBB|Replacements}} clone troopers were initially retained by the [[Imperial Army]] that replaced the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], but rumors spread throughout the ranks that the cloning facilities on Kamino had been shut down.[[Darth Vader (2017) 2|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 2]] ===Rise of volunteers and conscripts=== {{Quote|The city is filling up with soldiers in white armor. They call themselves STORMTROOPERS, and the Empire uses them to keep order on Lothal. They say they're here to protect us. What they're really here to protect are the factories, farms, and mines—to profit the Empire. They don't care about Lothal, or the people who work hard. They only care about what they're taking ''out'' of Lothal. What makes it worse is that, underneath those white stormtrooper helmets and black TIE fighter pilot helmets, a lot of the Imperials actually come from here. There are training academies set up now that turn good Lothal folks into soldiers of the Empire. I guess a lot of people here, being so used to living out on the edge of nowhere, signed up because they wanted to connect to something bigger. Can't they see what they're signing up for?|[[Ezra Bridger]]|''[[Star Wars Rebels: A New Hero]]''}} {{Main|TK stormtrooper}} [[File:Elite-Squad-Full.png|thumb|right|250px|Vice Admiral Rampart would organize a task force of Elite Squad Troopers, enlisted recruits who would be trained by elite clones such as Commander Crosshair.]] In the days following the end of the Clone Wars, [[Vice Admiral]] [[Edmon Rampart]] sanctioned the creation of an [[Elite Squad]] of non-clone human soldiers, led by the former [[Clone Force 99]] marksman [[Crosshair|CT-9904]] "Crosshair." Rampart envisioned enlisting human soldiers and having them train under skilled clones would be the best way to generate loyal soldiers without the cloning program. The squad included four highly skilled recruits enlisted to be the first wave of such soldiers. The individuals traded in their names for numbers, becoming [[ES-01]], [[ES-02]], [[ES-03]], and [[ES-04]] and undertaking early missions to eliminate insurgents throughout the galaxy,{{Databank|elite-squad|Elite Squad}} in particular, pursuing the now-rogue Clone Force 99, Crosshair's old squad. The squad's success during their missions proved the potential of enlistment as the method to fill the ranks of the Imperial Army to Tarkin, who allowed Rampart to continue secretly enlisting more recruits under [[Project War-Mantle]]. Though Tarkin supported Project War-Mantle, he believed the clone troopers would continue to remain essential until the Imperial Army was ready to retire them. [[File:EmpireMilitary-WM.png|thumb|left|300px|Clone stormtroopers were gradually supplanted as the Galactic Empire turned to the recruitment and conscription of birth-born human soldiers.]] With the development of the new Imperial war machine under Project War-Mantle,{{SWE|groups|empire|Galactic Empire}} a [[TK stormtrooper armor|new armor model]] was produced to be used by the enlisted recruits. Massive stockpiles of this armor was stored on planets such as [[Barton IV]] in preparation for the influx of future recruits in the Stormtrooper Corps. Clone [[commando]]s were deployed as instructors to the enlisted troopers, who were assigned the designation of [[TK stormtrooper]]s. During the first year of the Empire's reign, a [[Imperial Base on Daro|secret training facility]] had been set up on [[Daro]], where fifty clone commandos were tasked with training the first thousand TK stormtroopers. In order to fully cease clone production, Tarkin had Rampart [[Attack on Kamino|destroy]] Tipoca City with his [[Edmon Rampart's fleet|fleet]] of [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venators'']]. The continued recruitment of non-clone troops and the destruction of Kamino was kept secret from the [[Imperial Senate]], with the latter incident being covered up as the result of a cataclysmic storm.{{TBB|Truth and Consequences}} [[File:GrottonArrives-TBB203.png|thumb|right|300px|Recruited stormtroopers began to see increased deployment in the place of their clone forebears as Project War-Mantle carried on.]] Stormtroopers in armor that was[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]] close to the final design were deployed to the planet [[Mon Cala]], where they engaged the native [[Quarren]] and [[Mon Calamari]] in the Empire's [[Invasion of Mon Cala|planetary invasion]]. Also involved in the operation were clone troopers from the last Kaminoan batch, with the newly deployed clones having been assigned to Darth Vader and the [[Inquisitorius]] as a disposable death squad: the [[Purge Trooper]]s.[[Darth Vader (2017) 16|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 16]] Recruited stormtrooper soldiers were also deployed in the place of clones to worlds like the Outer Rim planet [[Thabeska]], the moon of [[Raada]],[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] and the Separatist planet [[Desix]] which in specific saw a large number of TK stormtroopers move into occupy its lands after a [[Crosshair and Cody's team|clone trooper squad]] claimed [[Desix City]] for the Empire with the squad's commanding officer, [[Clone Commander]] [[Cody]], watching in silence as the new soldiers took control. Cody had hoped to open diplomatic talks with Governor [[Tawni Ames]], only for her to be executed at the order of the newly appointed Imperial Governor [[Grotton]].{{TBB|The Solitary Clone}} Having also taken part in the [[Pacification of Kashyyyk|enslavement of Kashyyykk]],{{HelmetCollectionCite|35|Helmets}} Cody was unable to justify the Empire's actions and abandoned the Imperial Military. Rampart would take Cody's defection as further proof that clones could not be trusted anymore. [[File:StormingAbartolom-BattleOfJakkuInsurgencyRising1.png|thumb|left|250px|Once the Defense Recruitment Bill was approved by the Imperial Senate, TK stormtroopers would fully integrate into the Imperial Army, largely replacing clones as enforcers of the Empire.]] With funding for Project War-Mantle secured and preparations well underway, all that remained to be done was for the clone army to begin its gradual decommissioning. To accomplish this, Rampart proposed the [[Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill]] to the Imperial Senate, which would see the Imperial Military officially transition from the clone army to a recruitment one. Though many in the Senate saw the creation of a new army as unnecessary, others supported the idea especially after the destruction of Kamino meant that fresh clone troopers could no longer be produced to protect the Empire. Due to an inability to reach an agreement, the Bill was tabled multiple times. However, testimony from Senator [[Riyo Chuchi]] exposed Rampart for what he did and ultimately led to his arrest, seemingly shelving the Bill once more however, Palpatine appeared before the Senate and expressed his belief that clones could no longer be trusted to form the entirety of the Imperial Military due to the Attack on Kamino. With this development, the Senate passed the Bill. The passing of the Bill jeopardized the future of the clone stormtroopers, who still comprised the bulk of the Empire's forces during the early Imperial Era. Though the Bill proposed pensions for the clones as they would gradually be rotated out of military service as they aged, many troopers wished to continue their military service. [[File:Caysin_Bog_Trailer.png|thumb|right|250px|Stormtroopers spread throughout the galaxy as the new face of the Imperial regime, with recruits growing to outnumber the clones as the Galactic Empire grew and expanded.]] As the years passed, clone stormtroopers gradually became less and less common as many were either killed in action or rotated out of military service as they aged. As a result, the ranks of the Stormtrooper [[Corps]] swelled''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' with conscripts{{Databank|clone-veteran|Clone Veteran}} and volunteers, who sought to carry on the legacy of the clones that had been glorified through wartime [[propaganda]]. By the later Imperial Era, it was rumored the [[Stormtrooper Corps]] had been established within the Imperial [[Army]] by a group of former [[clone commando]]s.''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]'' Nonetheless, several clones remained in service to the Empire during its later years despite their advanced aging, with some becoming instructors in the [[Imperial Academy]],{{RebelsRecon|nARQwR5prTo|#2.02: Inside "The Lost Commanders" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-the-lost-commanders}} while a smaller number remained in active duty such as [[Sergeant]] [[Crest]], [[Crag]], and [[Torrent]], who was still active following the [[Battle of Yavin]]. ===The face of the Empire=== {{Quote|While we now consider the Imperial stormtrooper to have effectively been ever-present within the ranks of the military and on thousands of different worlds within the Empire, there was a time when they were relatively scarce. Stormtroopers were initially intended to be the elite corps of the new Imperial military. ''[…]'' By the time of the Galactic Civil War, however, stormtroopers had been almost entirely incorporated as the primary infantry of the Empire and were regularly deployed to systems across the galaxy, while also manning countless starships of the Imperial Navy.|[[Beaumont Kin]], ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''|''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''}} [[File:ImperialArmyBarricade-Andor112.png|thumb|left|250px|Stormtroopers were deployed alongside Imperial army troopers just before the outbreak of the Rix Road Riot on Ferrix.]] During the Emperor's reign, stormtroopers were used to bring any remaining Separatist [[Planet|worlds]] into line.''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' As [[time]] passed, stormtroopers replaced [[Imperial Army trooper]]s—the main [[infantry]] force of the early Empire, often consisting of local planetary defense forces conscripted into the [[Imperial Military]]—as mainline combat troops and security forces.''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' Becoming the Empire's foot soldiers,{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Jedi Temple Archives|cardname=Stormtroopers|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022642/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith-38-J-Stormtroopers}} the white armored troopers served as the backbone{{GOA|Stormtroopers vs. Rebels – Soldiers of the Galactic Empire}} and centerpiece''[[Ultimate Sticker Collection: Star Wars Vile Villains]]'' of the Empire's ground forces With a lack of jobs and opportunity in the wake of the Clone Wars, posterity would later come to criticize an "aimless generation" as complicit in abetting the rapid militarization and recruitment of the Imperial war machine: with an entire generation growing up under Imperial rule,{{StoryCite|story=The Final Order|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} a number of recruits had been indoctrinated into Imperial thinking since their childhood and thus joined with the Stormtrooper Corps willingly.''[[The Princess and the Scoundrel]]'' [[File:Officers_Harass_Merchant.png|thumb|right|250px|Stormtroopers would enforce Imperial law on occupied worlds, such as Lothal.]] Propaganda resulted in people from occupied planets joining into the Corps out of fear and with ambitions of power. Additionally, some stormtrooper recruits were people from disfranchised worlds who, by future Jedi Padawan [[Ezra Bridger]]'s reading of the situation, wanted to be part of something bigger than themselves and thus willingly joined the Empire. Bridger, however, was disturbed people from his homeworld [[Lothal]] would join with the Empire that changed their world. The Stormtrooper Corps training turned those who became stormtroopers into loyal followers of the Empire's will;''[[Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy]]'' while some stormtroopers would desert over the Empire's history,{{Andor|The Eye}} the Stormtrooper Corps was full of loyal Imperial soldiers who would kill any rebel they spotted, no matter the background from which they joined the corps. [[File:VaderLeading-2015DarthVader7.png|thumb|left|250px|Acting as Commander-in-Chief, Darth Vader often commanded stormtrooper legions.]] Informal [[Commander-in-Chief]]{{BustCollectionCite|30|Star Wars Universe}} [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] often coordinated the stormtroopers' operations in the field whenever his personal presence was required, with the stormtroopers addressing him by his noble title of [[Lord]].''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]'' The commitment the stormtroopers displayed to Vader bordered on worship.''[[Lords of the Sith]]'' Although he had a rapport with his stormtroopers,[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] Vader was still willing to execute the troops under his command[[Star Wars (2015) 2|''Star Wars'' (2015) 2]] as he did with many other subordinates. During [[Rae Sloane]]'s time as a [[junior officer]], a joke spread throughout the ranks that Vader only kept stormtroopers on the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of his [[starship]]s to drag out the bodies of those he executed. However, the joke lost all humor quickly, as the [[cyborg]]'s wrath became all too real for many of his subordinates.{{StoryCite|story=Lord Vader Will See You Now|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} [[File:Rebels_protect_Trayvis.png|thumb|right|250px|Stormtroopers on Lothal would combat the Specters, a local rebel cell, in multiple engagements.]] Per their swear to demonstrate absolute loyalty to the Empire in the Emperor's name, stormtroopers carried out some of the worst crimes committed by the Empire.''[[Star Wars Rebels: Rebels Versus Empire Ultimate Sticker Book]]'' Ultimately, stormtroopers came to represent the face of the Empire, but the soldiers were opposed by a growing{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}} [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebellion]] that sought to restore the rule of the Republic to the galaxy. On Lothal, the local [[Lothal garrison|stormtrooper garrison]] opposed Bridger and the [[Spectres]] rebel cell{{Rebels|Call to Action}} before the aspiring Jedi and his teammates joined the growing Rebellion. ===Galactic Civil War=== {{Quote|We follow orders. It's the sum and extend of our existence. Say kill, and we will. Say die, and our arms fly up and take the blasterfire on full. Watch our pointless existence extinguished on command.|Stormtrooper TD-7556|}} [[File:Expose_Pursue_Destroy.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Glorified in posters like ''[[Expose, Pursue, Destroy]]'', stormtroopers served in the Galactic Civil War, a conflict that the Empire ultimately lost.]] The [[Battle of Scarif]] was the first major rebel victory of the [[Galactic Civil War]], between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Following the Rebel victory at [[Scarif]],''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' Lord Vader commanded his stormtroopers to [[Secret mission to Tatooine|capture]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]]’s [[CR90 corvette|Alderaanian corvette]] ''[[Tantive IV]]'' over [[Tatooine]].{{Film|IV}} Additionally, Stormtroopers were also used to arrest dissidents on numerous worlds including [[Akiva]][[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] and [[Zeitooine]],''[[Lost Stars]]'' while they were also deployed to other conflicts the Empire found itself in; stormtroopers and Imperial machines quickly put down a [[Koshagan uprising|long-lasting uprising]] on [[Koshaga]],{{StoryCite|story=Beyond Hope|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} fought on the frontlines of the [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|Mandalorian Civil War]],''[[Star Wars Rebels: Heroes of Mandalore]]'' engaged the [[Dreamers]] and their [[Crunchers|man-eating pets]],''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]'' and combated members of the [[Grysk Hegemony]] during the [[Imperial–Grysk conflict]].''[[Thrawn: Alliances]]'' [[File:ImperialsAttackTatooineRebels-Commander.png|thumb|right|250px|Stormtroopers would combat the Rebel Alliance across the Galactic Civil War.]] As the Galactic Civil War dragged on, the Stormtrooper Corps accelerated its training to ensure the Empire had more troops at its disposal. For service in the Galactic Civil War, stormtroopers saw action against the Rebellion forces during engagements like the [[Battle of Garel]],{{Rebels|Legacy (episode)}} the [[Battle of Atollon]],{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} the [[Battle of Hoth]],{{Film|V}} the [[Mid Rim Retreat]], and the [[Battle of Ab Dalis]].[[Star Wars (2020) 15|''Star Wars'' (2020) 15]] Although desertion from the Stormtrooper Corps was rare,{{EncyclopediaCite|Imperial Troops}} the actions the Empire carried out during a [[mission on Aleen]] were so horrifying [[Unidentified stormtrooper deserter 1|three]] [[Unidentified stormtrooper deserter 2|stormtroopers]] [[Unidentified stormtrooper deserter 3|deserted]] the Imperial Army.{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=22|story=A Matter Of Perception}} Additionally, stormtroopers who served under [[Admiral]] [[Gratloe]] joined their officer's [[Gratloe's faction|rogue faction]] of the Empire in the [[Kudo system]], only for their faction to come into [[Mission to the Kudo system|conflict]] with the [[204th Imperial Fighter Wing]].[[TIE Fighter 2|''TIE Fighter'' 2]] [[File:EndorStrikeTeamCapture.jpg|thumb|left|250px|At Endor, a legion of the Emperor's best stormtroopers ambushed rebel forces attempting to destroy the Death Star II, though they would soon become overwhelmed by the native Ewoks who allied with the rebellion.]] Around the same time,[[TIE Fighter 5|''TIE Fighter'' 5]] an entire [[legion]] of Palpatine's best stormtroopers in the [[Battle of Endor]]{{Film|VI}} in [[4 ABY]].''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' As stormtroopers fought on the ground of the [[forest]] [[moon]] against Rebels and [[Ewok]]s, others were stationed aboard the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] before it was destroyed. In the immediate aftermath of the battle, Rebel General [[Han Solo]] led an [[Assault on an Imperial outpost|assault]] against a [[Imperial outpost (Endor)|surviving Endor outpost]] staffed by stormtroopers,[[Shattered Empire 1|''Shattered Empire'' 1]] while stormtroopers on Imperial [[capital]] world of [[Coruscant]] fought in the planet's [[Coruscant civil war|civil war]] that began directly after the deaths of Palpatine and Vader at [[Endor]]. [[File:Remnant-Stormtroopers.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The rise of the New Republic drove stormtroopers to the galaxy's outer reaches where they found work as mercenaries.]] In the years that followed the civil war's conclusion, all that seemingly remained of the former Galactic Empire were the [[Mercenary|mercenaries]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}} many stormtroopers had become{{GentleGiantCite|set=Mini Busts|pack=Remnant Trooper|link=star-wars-the-mandalorian-remnant-trooper-mini-bust}}—known as "Remnant Stormtroopers"{{Databank|stormtroopers|Stormtroopers|oldversion=20200807132423}} {{C|version archived on August 7, 2020; now replaced}} or "Remnant Troopers"—and the [[warlord]]s who tried to carve out their own territory, with Remnant Stormtroopers appearing under them, clinging to the last vestiges of Imperial power in the [[Outer Rim Territories]], where the New Republic held little influence.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}} Despite the restrictions that the New Republic imposed on the defeated Empire, stormtroopers retained their battle-worn [[Stormtrooper armor|armor]], making them look like an undisciplined mercenary force. After Djarin took out the two fighters, he and Grogu departed for [[Tython]]. =====All roads lead to Grogu===== Unaware that one of Gideon's agents, a [[Unidentified Mimbanese worker|Mimbanese worker]] undercover on Nevarro, had placed a [[Homing beacon|tracker]] on the ''Razor Crest'', Djarin ended up leading Gideon to Tython, where the Mandalorian was involved in a standoff with former bounty hunter Boba Fett and [[Master Assassin]] [[Fennec Shand]] over [[Boba Fett's armor|Fett's armor]], which Djarin [[Mission to Tatooine (Din Djarin)|acquired]] on Tatooine, while Grogu mediated{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} and made contact with Luke Skywalker. However, a [[missile]] from Fett's armor, which the former hunter reclaimed from the ''Razor Crest'', destroyed both fleeing transports, wiping out the surviving stormtroopers. However, a team of [[Phase-III Dark Trooper|third-generation design Dark Troopers]] managed to capture Grogu and deliver him to Gideon's light cruiser, which then destroyed the ''Razor Crest''. [[File:Stormtroopers-salute.png|thumb|right|270px|Stormtroopers served within a grouping of remnants on the world of Morak, where they unknowingly welcomed undercover enemies Din Djarin and Migs Mayfield.]] Returning to Nevarro aboard Fett's ''[[Slave I]]'' starship and recruiting Dune to the new [[Second rescue of Grogu|mission to rescue Grogu]], the Mandalorian and his allies recruited former Imperial sniper{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}} [[Migs Mayfeld]] and [[Mission to Morak|infiltrated]] the Morak Imperial remnants, which were based out of a [[Imperial refinery|refinery]] working to refine [[rhydonium]] to use against the New Republic. The united Mandalorians, however, managed to overcome Gideon's forces, with Djarin and Grogu wiping out his clone army before the Moff himself perished in the destruction of his base. Afterward, the New Republic was made aware of Gideon's activity on Mandalore and subsequent demise.{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}} ====The army of Thrawn==== =====Survival in the wilds===== The return of Thrawn promised to galvanize the Imperial remnants.{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}} While many Imperial remnants were already secretly networked under the Shadow Council, their forces lacked proper leadership and remained divided by the council's squabbling, with Captain [[Gilad Pellaeon]] holding back efforts to unite by promising Thrawn would soon return which would herald in the reemergence of the Imperial Military and give fellow council member [[Commandant]] [[Brendol Hux]] enough time to complete the late [[Chief Scientist]] [[Doctor]] [[Royce Hemlock]]’s [[Project Necromancer]]. However, since the [[Liberation of Lothal]], Thrawn had remained trapped in [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] in [[Far galaxy|another galaxy]], where he remained on the planet [[Peridea]] with a [[Thrawn's forces|grouping of stormtrooper forces]] thanks to the actions of Bridger and the [[Purrgil]] star [[whale]]s. In time, Thrawn's stormtrooper forces had dwindled to only a [[Thrawn's Night Trooper legion|legion's]] worth{{ThisWeek|lxo8qzDZM4E|Dispatch: Far, Far Away|sw_url=video/far-far-away-this-week-in-star-wars-dispatch}} of stormtroopers. [[File:NightTrooperArmy.png|thumb|right|300px|Night Troopers were a dedicated legion of stormtroopers who served Thrawn during his exile.]] However, Thrawn's Imperial remnant also allied with the [[Great Mothers]] of the long since fallen [[Witch Kingdom of the Dathmiri]], whom Thrawn found slumbering within a [[Great Mothers' Fortress|Dathomiri fortress]]. After joining forces with the three [[Nightsisters]], Thrawn and his forces began rebuilding their Star Destroyer, the ''[[Chimaera]]'', as part of a plan to return home with their aid.{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}} The [[Great Mothers]] energized Thrawn's stormtroopers, who became inhumanely persistent{{Databank|night-troopers|Night Troopers}} and adopted the name "[[Night Trooper]]s,"{{Ahsoka|Part Six: Far, Far Away}} {{C|[[Disney+]] subtitles}} which was similar to the "[[Nightsisters|Nightsister]]" name used by the [[Dathomirian|Dathomiri]]. The legion was placed under [[Captain]] [[Enoch]], who served as the [[Captain of the Guard|leader of Thrawn's death trooper guard]]. Beyond energizing Thrawn's living soldiers, the Great Mothers also had access to the [[Chant of Resurrection]], which would enable them to reanimate any soldier who died. However, no Night Trooper was ever resurrected in front of Bridger, who avoided the Nightsister fortress and made a life for himself among the [[Noti]]. Two members of [[Thrawn's guard|Thrawn's death trooper guard]] were reanimated at some point. By 9 ABY,{{AhsokaSeriesDate}} Thrawn had, through the Great Mothers, managed to reach out to his servant Magistrate [[Morgan Elsbeth]], herself a former Nightsister at the head of a [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|remnant]] in the main galaxy.{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} It became Elsbeth's responsibility to deliver Thrawn and his forces from exile, with Thrawn promising the Great Mothers he would bring them and cargo from their catacombs to the main galaxy with him. Assembling a massive [[Hyperspace transport ring]] dubbed the ''[[Eye of Sion]]'' through Imperial loyalists at her old factory on Corellia, Elsbeth led her forces, among them mercenaries [[Baylan Skoll]] and his apprentice [[Shin Hati]], on an intergalactic hyperspace journey to the other galaxy after a [[Incident on Seatos|skirmish]] with former Jedi [[Ahsoka Tano]], her Mandalorian Padawan [[Sabine Wren]], their droid [[Huyang]], and New Republic forces.{{Ahsoka|Part Four: Fallen Jedi}} With Wren, Morgan and her allies united with the Great Mothers, Thrawn, and his stormtroopers on Peridea. As per his agreement with the Great Mothers, Thrawn ordered Enoch to have his stormtroopers start bringing the Great Mothers' cargo into the ''Chimaera'' since Elsbeth predicted the cargo transfer would take at least three rotations with the Grand Admiral thinking that was an acceptable timeframe. =====Delaying the enemy===== [[File:Ahsoka7-croppedvariant-Reis.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Night Troopers cross paths with Ezra Bridger once more during the skirmish on Peridea.]] With their arrival, Elsbeth's forces fell under Thrawn's command, with Enoch exercising command over her [[RP82 Fiend fighter|Fiend starfighter units]]. Allowing Wren to venture into the wilderness to find Bridger, Thrawn also prepared two attack squads to follow Skoll and Hati to ensure Wren and Bridger were killed, declining Elsbeth's suggestion to send more soldiers because of his numbers. In time, Tano and Huyang would also arrive above Peridea with a purrgil pod, although Thrawn, who entered into his command center under the guard of two Night Troopers, had Enoch call off a starfighter attack to play the long game and avoid wasting their [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|few]] [[Thrawn's Night Trooper legion|resources]]. Two Night Troopers continued to stand guard in Thrawn's command center as the Great Mothers found Tano's position in the debris field around Peridea, giving the ''Eye of Sion''{{'s}} under Enoch's command a chance to fire on her position and flush her out of hiding. While their fighters again pursued Tano's T-6 shuttle, which was heading far from Thrawn's position anyway to reunite with Wren, Hati reported Bridger's position and led the local [[Bandits of Peridea]] against the mobile Noti tribe, while Skoll departed his apprentice's company in pursuit of a great power connected to the [[The Ones|Mortis gods]]. Dispatched on Thrawn's order and arriving after the bandits had been taken out, the two prepared Night Trooper squads—[[Team One]] and [[Team Two]]—arrived on [[LAAT/le patrol gunship]]s and reinforced Hati, surrounding Bridger and Wren under the counter-encirclement tandem. Quickly falling under Hati's command while Thrawn kept watch from afar via a droid, the stormtroopers ignored Bridger's attempts to negotiate and engaged Wren, Bridger, and the newly-arrived Tano. Without Skoll's assistance, Hati and the Night Troopers were overwhelmed by the three Jedi, forcing Thrawn to withdraw his troops and the starfighters pursuing the T-6, currently piloted by Huyang. The Night Troopers abandoned Hati, who fled on her [[howler]] mount. =====Escape from Peridea===== {{Quote|''[To the Night Troopers]'' The blessing of the Great Mothers shall protect you in battle against the Jedi. That attack grounded the shuttle—forcing Tano, Wren, and Bridger to race for the Nightsister fortress on howlers—and was reported to Thrawn, who prepared for their incoming ground assault. Told they had the "blessing" of the Great Mothers by Elsbeth and ordered to let no-one through, those Night Troopers remained in position for Tano, Wren, and Bridger. [[File:EzraStrikesUndeadNightTroopers-Ahsoka.png|thumb|right|300px|The corpses of fallen Night Troopers arise thanks to the Chant of Resurrection and march against the Jedi attackers.]] With Enoch and Elsbeth by his side, while the room remained guarded by two Night Troopers, Thrawn ordered the ''Chimarea'' to [[aerial bombardment|aerially bombard]] the incoming Jedi, all of whom managed to survive. With their enemies closing in, the Night Trooper volunteers were dispatched to the fortress's lower levels and engaged the Jedi, who tricked the stormtroopers into drawing themselves out and thus took out the entire force. The corpses of the volunteers, however, were reanimated by the Great Mothers' use of the Chant of Resurrection, much to the shock of the three Jedi, who were unable to injure the reanimated soldiers. The reanimated stormtroopers cracked their own bones as they arose and let out a number of undead groans{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}} {{C|[[Disney+]] subtitles}} in pursuit of the Jedi, who sealed the undead behind heavy doors the Night Troopers needed to cut their way through. To protect the ''Chimaera'', Thrawn's two undead death troopers kept Wren and Bridger from the departing destroyer's hangar at the top of the fortress while Tano dueled Elsbeth. The zombified death troopers managed to hold off Bridger and Wren as Thrawn, taking command of the ''Eye of Sion'' from its bridge with Enoch and the Great Mothers at his side, began his departure. =====Return to the known galaxy===== [[File:ThrawnEnochSion-PartEight.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Beginning a new period of strife for the New Republic, Grand Admiral Thrawn and the stormtroopers under his command managed to escape to the galaxy during the battle of Peridea.]] [[LS-757]] and another Night Trooper were stationed in the ''Chimaera''{{'s}} hangar when Wren, who managed to unlock her Force-sensitivity in the battle, and Bridger finally bested the death troopers. Moving to the edge of the hangar, both stormtroopers rushed to defend the ''Chimaera'' but quickly assumed they were safe because of the distance between the starship and the fortress. Wren, however, helped Bridger cross the divide with a Force push; LS-757 and the other trooper were unsure if the Jedi had made the jump until he leaped up from his landing place, quickly throwing the second trooper from the ''Chimaera'' before Wren [[Death|shot]] LS-757 from her distance below. Meanwhile, the zombified Night Troopers had broken through the last of the doors and joined Elsbeth in attacking Tano, whom Wren stayed behind to help. The undead soldiers stayed back as Elsbeth engaged Tano atop the tower until Wren revealed herself; as the apprentice distracted the undead Night Troopers, Tano finished her duel with Elsbeth and slayed the Nightsister, whose death was felt by the Great Mother [[Klothow]] and thus reported to Thrawn. With the distance between the ''Chimaera'' and tower only having increased, Bridger was unable to go back for his friends and could only watch their battle with the zombie Night Troopers until an officer contacted LS-757 with news of incoming reinforcements. Bridger reacted quickly and took the trooper's suit of armor. While the news came as a shock to Klothow, Thrawn ordered the ''Chimaera'' to bombard the Nightsister fortress below, which was destroyed and took the undead Night Troopers with it. Wren and Tano, however, managed to escape when Huyang arrived in the T-6 in time. However, after Thrawn delivered a final message to Tano, the ''Eye of Sion'' and attached ''Chimaera'' would ultimately escape into hyperspace before the T-6 could catch up. Thrawn and his forces were thus delivered out of exile and returned to the main galaxy; while Bridger managed to slip away in LS-757's armor aboard an [[Baylan's shuttle|''Eta''-class shuttle]] previously used by Hati and Skoll, the ''Chimaera'' made its way to the Nightsister planet{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}} of [[Dathomir]] with the Great Mothers and their cargo safely aboard. While the appearance of a figure in stormtrooper armor did cause concern before he revealed his face, Bridger, meanwhile, made his way to ''Home One'' and met up with the New Republic. ===Legacy=== ====Opinions==== {{Dialogue|Ranzar Malk|Yeah, well, Mayfeld, he's… He's one of the best triggermen I've ever seen. Former Imperial sharpshooter.|Din Djarin|That's not saying much.|Migs Mayfeld|I wasn't a stormtrooper, wiseass.|attr=Ranzar Malk, Din Djarin, and Migs Mayfeld|src=}} Opinions on the combat skills of stormtroopers and their overall quality varied to some degree both during the Empire's reign and after it collapsed. [[Commander]] [[Alecia Beck]] praised the stormtroopers, calling them the Empire's "keenest weapon." [[Jedi Master|Master]] Kenobi once noted the accuracy and precision of their blaster shots, while Knight [[Kanan Jarrus]] mocked stormtroopers as soldiers with poor aim.{{Rebels|Stealth Strike}} Stormtrooper [[Sardis Ramsin|TD-7556]] claimed it was the standard issue E-11 blaster that hampered a stormtrooper's aim in his mockingly written final report before deserting, while [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] regarded the stormtroopers themselves as the problem. [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] defended the stormtroopers for their allegiance to the Empire, but Rex took the opportunity to disparage them as an inferior class of soldier relative to the genetically engineered clone troopers they replaced.{{Rebels|Relics of the Old Republic}} [[File:Scoundrels-Rebels-Empire-AmazonCover.png|thumb|right|250px|Stormtroopers were remembered as a symbol of Imperial oppression, but opinions on and claims about their overall efficiency, particularly their aim, varied.]] During the earliest days of stormtrooper recruitment and training, Clone Commando Sergeant Hunter of Clone Force 99 noted the apparent ineffectiveness of the recruits at the time, with clone commando Gregor claiming he purposely avoided teaching the new soldiers everything he knew. Thinking about rebel propaganda that portrayed Imperial servants as poor shots, [[fleet logistics liaison]] [[Arvira]] of the Imperial Navy claimed that some stormtroopers should indeed spend more time practicing their targeting drills.{{StoryCite|story=The Sith of Datawork|book=From a Certain Point of View}} [[Tasu Leech]], a [[Fighting pit|pit]] fighter and rising star in the criminal underworld during the Galactic Civil War,[[Bounty Hunters 8|''Bounty Hunters'' 8]] was aware of claims about poor stormtrooper marksmanship and used them to mock a [[Unidentified coastal defender stormtrooper (Bestine IV)|shoretrooper]] holding a blaster to his head, putting his life on the line in the name of mocking his captor. The shoretooper responded by headbutting the bounty hunter, retorting that their aim with the strike was direct, before being killed by the defecting Imperial Lieutenant [[Beilert Valance]].[[Bounty Hunters 31|''Bounty Hunters'' 31]] In truth, the overall difference in stormtrooper aim and training varied between individual troopers across the galaxy.''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' While a majority of troopers across the galaxy possessed an overall superb aim, with Imperial specialist [[Ralsius Paldora]] stating that stormtroopers hit 77 percent of their targets, rebel propaganda and the soldiers who demonstrated lackluster aim created the joke that all troopers possessed poor marksmanship. The joke outlived the regime itself. Following the Imperial Era, Din Djarin, himself a skilled Mandalorian warrior trained since a young age, held stormtroopers in low regard relative to Mandalorians, being unimpressed by Migs Mayfeld's military background despite [[Ranzar Malk]]'s assurance that the Imperial veteran was skilled in marksmanship. Mayfeld, an ex-[[Imperial sharpshooter]] who participated in Operation: Cinder, retorted that he was not a stormtrooper. [[Axe Woves]], another skilled Mandalorian warrior who supported Bo-Katan Kryze, mocked the remnant stormtroopers of Gideon's remnant, joking that they lacked true marksmanship.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} ====Symbol of a fallen empire==== {{Quote|Oh, I think I understand, Synara. My Great Grand-Nikto told me about the Empire. There were stories of the stormtroopers not being very nice to our people.|[[Neeku Vozo]], to [[Synara San]]|{{Resistance|The First Order Occupation}}}} [[File:TheMandalorianChapter5.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The remnants of stormtrooper helmets left on pikes outside of Mos Eisley on Tatooine.]] The stormtrooper became a symbol of the Empire across the galaxy, resulting in their blank armor persisting as a representation of the regime after its fall.''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian: The Manga]]'' On Tatooine, citizens celebrated the death of Palpatine and later fall of the Empire. In the liberated [[spaceport]] city of [[Mos Eisley]], the helmets of stormtroopers were left on pikes{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 5: The Gunslinger}} by 9 ABY. After the space station's destruction in the Battle of Endor, the [[Death Star ruins|ruins of the Death Star II]] settled within the waters of [[Kef Bir]], a moon in the [[Endor system]]. As the years passed, the armor of deceased stormtroopers remained abandoned within the ruins, growing dirty with age and water damage.{{Film|IX}} In the New Republic's [[The Pilots' Rest Quonset hut|Adelphi Base lounge]],{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}} {{AD|Disney+}} stormtrooper helmets were included amongst the war trophies the [[Adelphi Rangers]] kept above their bar. Stormtrooper armor did get a new purpose on the former Imperial world of [[Plazir-15]], where the elected monarchy's [[Plazir-15 Security Detail|secruity detail]] wore former stormtrooper gear, albeit without helmets and with planetary robes.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 22: Guns for Hire}} One Ewok also wore a stormtrooper helmet while fighting in the [[Ewok Civil War]].{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-dark-horse|text=SWCE 2023: Dark Horse Reveals a ''Star Wars: The High Republic Adventures'' Phase III Teaser, New Jaxxon Art, and More}} Nevertheless, the armor remained a symbol of the Empire and its ideals for the galaxy at large over the following decades.[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] By [[28 ABY]],{{Twitter|DelReyStarWars|status/652893780236988420|[[Del Rey]]|quote=So excited to have @claudiagray writing a #StarWars novel with us. SW: New Republic: Bloodline coming 2016. Set 6 years before TFA.|archivefile=File:New Republic Bloodline Twitter Post.jpg}} establishes that the events of [[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] take place six [[Standard year|years]] before the events of {{Film|VII}}. ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of ''The Force Awakens'' to [[34 ABY]], so ''Bloodline'' must take place in [[28 ABY]]. stormtrooper helmets and armor were collected by individuals like the New Republic [[senator]] [[Ransolm Casterfo]], who had an interest in Imperial "artifacts." Several of Casterfo's [[Centrists|Centrist]] senators, including [[Ormes Apolin]] and [[Fatil]] also admired and collected Imperial uniforms and armor. In addition, Imperial armor and other artifacts also sold at markets on [[Chrome Citadel]]. Stories of how the stormtroopers treated the [[Nikto]] species were passed down as a warning of Imperial xenophobia. ====The next generation==== {{Quote|Upon its emergence, the First Order deliberately invoked imagery unseen for a generation. The skull-like monochromatic visage of the stormtrooper—a clear evolution of an Imperial design—figured prominently.|[[Janyor]] of Bith|}} {{Main|First Order stormtrooper}} [[File:HuxAndStormtroopersAtCommandCenter-TFAOfficialTeaser.jpg|thumb|right|250px|During the New Republic Era, a new generation of stormtroopers was trained to serve the First Order.]] The Imperial remnants that retreated to the Unknown Regions reorganized themselves as the [[First Order]], achieving one of the Emperor's objectives—to destroy the Empire and then rebuild it—under the [[Contingency]].''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' Defying the Galactic Concordance, the First Order recruited and mobilized [[First Order stormtrooper|new stormtroopers]]. The new stormtroopers were influenced by the idea of Brendol. The First Order's stormtroopers were equipped with sleeker armor and powerful weaponry. Among the Order's agents was Terex, who had served as an Imperial stormtrooper. The former Imperial [[Stormtrooper Commander]] [[Ruthford]], who had been at the disposal of the Emperor's Fist during a [[battle against the Benathy]], served as a Captain in the First Order. Captain Ruthford would find himself [[Battle against the Benathy (First Order)|seeing]] the [[Benathy]] once again, although this time he served under the grandson of Lord Vader, the [[warlord]] [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]].[[Age of Resistance - Kylo Ren 1|''Age of Resistance - Kylo Ren'' 1]] ==Training== {{Quote|Cadets, you entered this facility as children. And in a few short weeks, you will leave as soldiers. By the time you complete your training, you will be prepared to serve your Emperor.|[[Cumberlayne Aresko]]|{{Rebels|Breaking Ranks}}}} [[File:Nothing_Beats_an_Academy_Education.png|thumb|left|230px|Stormtroopers were trained in Imperial Academies and subjected to numbing routine.]] Unlike their predecessors, the majority of stormtroopers were non-clone recruits. [[Imperial cadet]]s were shipped off to Imperial Academies, and subjected to rigorous training programs in order to produce highly trained shock troopers fiercely loyal to the Empire. Cadets could be as young as thirteen standard years.''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' Although they were a somewhat rare sight, [[Gender|women]] were not prohibited from serving in the ranks of the stormtroopers.[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']] During training, female [[cadet]]s were placed in all-female units. [[Unit Forn]] was an all-female unit at the [[Academy for Young Imperials]] on [[Lothal]].''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]'' All stormtroopers swore themselves to the Emperor and his will, with the expectation to follow all orders without question in the name of serving the Empire and Palpatine himself. Learning to obey all orders without concern was a part of stormtrooper training.''[[Ultimate Sticker Collection: Star Wars Rebels: Deadly Battles]]'' Stormtroopers were trained to disregard fallen comrades in battle and to press on, no matter the cost, even when the odds were stacked against them. In fact, those who were selected for stormtrooper training had to undergo extra reconditioning. This had the effect of dehumanizing the cadets, who came to refer to themselves by their [[operating number]]s rather than their names. One such cadet was [[Ames Bunkle]], an acquaintance of [[Zare Leonis]]. Minister [[Pitina Mar-Mas Voor]] of the Imperial [[Coalition for Progress]] regarded stormtroopers as brainwashed agents who were not as efficient as her division.[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 29|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 29]] [[File:Breaking_Ranks.png|thumb|right|250px|The stormtrooper training program promoted competition, ruthlessness, and unwavering loyalty to the Galactic Empire.]] Stormtrooper recruits trained in numerous conditions, including [[jetpack]] scenarios.''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]'' Among other things, cadets would train to fire [[blaster]]s, and Imperial specialist Ralsius Paldora noted that stormtroopers hit 77 percent of their targets. Cadets also learned to pilot [[Walker|Imperial walkers]] and the ruthlessness it took to become a stormtrooper. Cadets who attended Imperial Academies also underwent simulated obstacle courses in [[the Well]], which were designed to test their strength, agility, reflexes and intelligence. Such courses and tests of skill became increasingly difficult over time, and accountability for losses were harsh. While cadets attended the academy, they wore white uniforms and specialized helmets, similar to the standard stormtrooper or pilot gear. Aside from their basic training, many cadets were also assigned other non-combat duties on base. Such duties offered cadets the opportunity to gain experience over their peers, and were often presented as rewards for excellent performance during training exercises. [[File:The_Grand_Inquisitor_and_Zare_Leonis.png|thumb|left|250px|Stormtrooper cadets who exhibited a strong connection to the Force were reassigned to Project Harvester.]] As cadets were being evaluated, the officers in charge were often instructed to take note of performance that might denote an affinity for [[the Force]], and report it to one of their superiors. Cadets who met this special criteria were taken by [[the Grand Inquisitor]] and forcibly inducted into [[Project Harvester]], a top secret Imperial program based on [[Arkanis]]. Cadet Zare's older sister, [[Dhara Leonis]], was one known subject of Project Harvester. Another prospective subject was [[Jai Kell]], who managed to escape due to the help of [[Ezra Bridger]]. Stormtrooper and other Imperial cadets also assisted in law enforcement operations. Following a spate of rebel activity on Lothal, Imperial cadets there were used to search homes and streets for illegal activities, detain the children of fugitives, and to raid smugglers. During these law enforcements operations, some cadets, like [[Nazhros Oleg]] came to flout their new-found powers; a trait that was encouraged by some officers, like [[Captain]] [[Piers Roddance]]. Some prospective officer cadets, like Leonis and Oleg were also given the chance to lead adult stormtroopers in these raids. Cadets also had their backgrounds investigated for any sign of criminal connections and other subversive activities.''[[Servants of the Empire: Imperial Justice]]'' ==Equipment== ===Armor=== {{Quote|Gone were the flags, braids, baldrics, swords, and other regalia of tradition. They were replaced with a uniform look embodied by the stormtrooper.|Janyor|}} [[File:ImperialCloneArmy.png|thumb|right|300px|Clone stormtroopers retained their Phase II clone trooper armor during the early years of the Imperial Era.]] The clone troopers who survived the Clone Wars continued to wear the [[Phase II clone trooper armor]] after becoming the first generation of stormtroopers. The [[armor]] consisted of white [[plastoid]] plates attached to a black [[body glove]],{{Databank|clone-trooper-armor|Clone Trooper Armor}} no longer featuring the various color patterns{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/aftermath-episode-guide|text="Aftermath" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} Trivia Gallery that the clones had adopted after growing more individualistic under the Jedi Order's influence, although some units such as the [[Imperial shock trooper]]s still wore their armor with the distinctive red markings of the [[Coruscant Guard]]. The first non-clone stormtroopers, designated as [[TK stormtrooper]]s, were given an updated version of trooper armor as the Galactic Empire shifted toward willingly enlisted and unwillingly conscripted personnel alike[[The Mandalorian: The Manga, Vol. 2|''The Mandalorian: The Manga'', Vol. 2]] at the expense of clone soldiers. Like its clone armor templates, the [[TK stormtrooper armor]] was a set of white armor components worn over a black body glove. In addition to various aesthetic differences between the two armors, the TK [[helmet]] lacked the T-shaped visor of its Phase II predecessor and the earlier [[Phase I clone trooper armor]]. [[File:Future-stormtrooper-and-current-trooper.png|thumb|left|250px|During the Imperial Era, the white-armored stormtroopers became a symbol of the Galactic Empire.]] Phase II was ultimately phased out after the creation of [[stormtrooper armor]], causing large stocks of clone armor to be recycled as most clones entered retirement, having been replaced by natural-born soldiers. Stormtrooper armor was a common sight throughout the galaxy; its stark white appearance served as a symbol of the New Order in contrast to the clone armor that represented honor and defense during the Clone Wars. Stormtrooper armor was a distinctive set of white armor that was intended to instill a sense of order and security in loyal subjects and a sense of fear in the opponents of the Empire, while also providing the soldiers with an extended range of survival equipment and temperature controls. It was able to mitigate the effect of blaster fire and thus provide some protection; in certain cases, stormtroopers continued to breathe after being shot by an [[E-11 medium blaster rifle]].{{Rebels|Stealth Strike}} Projectiles from crude [[slugthrower]]s were unable to pierce the armor.{{StoryCite|story=The Final Order|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} Stormtrooper armor was not without the limitations common to most types of armor, however. The plates made running slightly harder and offered reduced protection against large scale pulse detonations and blunt weapons.''[[Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger]]'' Stormtroopers also had a utility belt and a grappling hook attached to it. Regardless, the armor was effective in mitigating most primary and secondary dangers in most combat scenarios. The helmet provided cranial protection, filtered [[Atmosphere|air]], and contained enhanced vision, communication systems and an effective''[[Battlefront II: Inferno Squad]]'' [[Heads-up display|HUD (heads up display)]] that could help locate threats, aid in navigation, and to help alert the wearer. While many stormtroopers deployed to such environments would retain their standard-issue white-colored armor, some stormtroopers involved in forest operations would wear a [[Camo stormtrooper armor|suit of camouflaged armor]], where the standard-issue white was painted over with a greenery inspired design that blended into nature. Rank was determined by a [[color]] coded [[pauldron]] worn over the right shoulder, with orange or red representing the rank of commander, black indicating an enlisted trooper, and white representing a sergeant. Sometimes on the pauldrons they had specific symbols distinguishing who they were serving, exemplified by [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn's]] troops, who had a stylized [[Chimaera (symbol)|chimaera symbol]] on their pauldrons.{{Rebels|Through Imperial Eyes}} ===Weapons=== [[File:GalaxyofAdventures-Stormtroopers.png|thumb|right|250px|E-11 blaster rifles were standard-issue weapons for Imperial stormtroopers.]] The E-11 blaster rifle was the standard issue weapon of stormtroopers,{{Databank|e-11-blaster-rifle|E-11 Blaster Rifle}} although the first generations—primarily clone stormtroopers and TK stormtroopers—used Clone War-era weapons such as the [[DC-15A blaster carbine]]. Stormtroopers also occasionally utilized the [[SE-14r light repeating blaster]],[[Star Wars (2020) 19|''Star Wars'' (2020) 19]] the [[DLT-20A blaster rifle]],''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' the [[T-21 light repeating blaster]], the [[RT-97C heavy blaster rifle]], the [[E-22 reciprocating double-barreled blaster rifle]], or the [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle]], especially for long range engagements. They could also use [[scatter gun]]s, and [[MPL-57]] [[grenade launcher]]s.''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'' Some stormtroopers were trained to handle [[HH-12 rocket launcher]]s{{Legion|set=Stormtroopers Unit Expansion}} or the [[T-7 ion disruptor rifle]].{{FFGTCG|set=A Wretched Hive|cardname=T-7 Ion Disruptor|link=opposition-cycle/a-wretched-hive/t-7-ion-disruptor-r1813}} ===Dress uniform=== Outside of combat and security details, stormtrooper officers wore black dress tunics, caps, and boots, as well as [[code cylinder]]s, [[rank insignia plaque]]s, [[officer's disk]]s conform to the [[Imperial military uniforms|standards]] of the Imperial Navy. ==Specialized stormtroopers== ===Overview=== {{Quote|There is no environment too deadly for a trooper. Wherever the Empire needs us, we'll be there!|Sentinel|''[[Star Wars: Hunters]]''}} [[File:SecretMission-Stormtroopers.png|thumb|left|350px|As the Empire was a galaxy-wide regime that constantly expanded, waged conflict on distant worlds, or ruled over those planets, different stormtrooper variants were created in order to maintain Imperial rule across any environment.]] In his Grand Arena persona as an Imperial loyalist, the former stormtrooper Sentinel once proclaimed that there should be no environment too deadly for an Imperial trooper, instead declaring that a trooper should go to wherever the Empire needed them to go.
